st.headline: Asian markets dip as investors weigh tech earnings, Gulf tensions
st.teaser: Concerns over AI and uncertainty in the Gulf lingered.
fullText: HONG KONG – Asian stocks struggled to stay above water in early trade on Oct 22 , as tech earnings optimism provided only fleeting support amid lingering concerns over AI and uncertainty in the Gulf .

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 0.2%, on track for a fourth straight week of decline. Japan’s Nikkei stock index gave up earlier gains to trade 0.4% lower, while South Korean shares were down more than 1%.
US stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis, were down 0.4% at 7,765.8.

Overnight, the tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close as better-than-expected earnings reports from market heavyweights helped ease some concerns over the sustainability and profitability of massive AI build-outs.

SpaceX posted its first profit as a public company, Meta reported third-quarter revenue that beat expectations, while AI server maker Super Micro forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin that both topped estimates.
However, Meta’s plan to issue non-voting Class C common stock drew renewed scrutiny on AI spending.
“There’s a lot of noise out there at the moment and investors are still digesting this morning’s results,” said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com

“Also, we’re really only at the start of the meaty part of earnings season, which is coming at the same time that investors are tackling the uncertainty from an upcoming Fed decision, geopolitical risks, and US mid-terms.”
In a sign of subdued risk sentiment, the yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes was down 4.2 basis points at 5.1065%, while the yield on 30-year notes was at a one-week low of 5.3968%.
Meanwhile, Brent crude rose 1.1% to US$110.03 a barrel, near a five-month high.

The US ordered diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes, while the New York Times reported the US and Israeli militaries had developed specific plans for renewed attacks on Iran after the US midterm elections, which take place on Nov 3.
In currencies, the dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies of other major trading partners, dipped to 102.2. The euro was little changed at US$1.1231.

The yen was also flat at 158.125, after Deputy Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino signalled his readiness to raise borrowing costs. The Korean won was muted at 1325.9, after the Bank of Korea left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.00% on Oct 22 .
Gold was slightly lower at US$4115.5 per ounce.
Bitcoin was down 0.4% at US$84,284.05, while ether was 0.6% lower at US$2,476.34. REUTERS

cna.headline: South Korea's celebrity shark back in canal, prompting new rescue bid
cna.teaser: The shark - nicknamed Bukhangi by fans - has drawn more than 1.6 million visitors to a canal in South Korea’s Busan since it was first spotted there last month.
fullText: SEOUL: A shark that became a viral sensation after getting stuck in a South Korean canal returned hours after being coaxed out, authorities said on Thursday (Oct 22), prompting another attempt to guide it back to the sea.

The shark - nicknamed Bukhangi by fans - was first spotted in the artificial waterway in the southeastern port city of Busan last month, with environmental activists linking its appearance to climate change.
Officials initially opted to wait for the shark to leave on its own, but took a more proactive approach amid growing concerns for its well-being.
Workers used nets fixed to floating pontoons late on Wednesday to guide the animal gradually, but it dived beneath a net and returned to the canal overnight, authorities said.
She said a fresh attempt began on Thursday morning, with authorities raising the outer net to allow Bukhangi to move from the canal.
Before Wednesday, authorities had twice tried and failed to steer Bukhangi back to sea, using water jets and then nets.
The three-metre "dusky" shark, a species typically found in tropical climates, amassed a huge following, drawing more than 1.6 million people to the Busan canal for a glimpse.
It has been celebrated for its unexpected boost to the local economy, with Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo thanking it for generating publicity he said would otherwise have cost "trillions".
But environmental groups link its initial appearance in the canal to warming seas, saying rising temperatures are pushing warm-water fish northwards, with subtropical sharks following in pursuit.

mom.headline: Additional Guidance for Employers on Use of 1-Hour PM2.5 Readings to Protect Outdoor Workers During Haze
mom.teaser: 1 The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has issued new guidance on how employers should adjust outdoor work based on the 1-hour PM2.5 readings. This complements the existing guidance based on the PSI forecast, and helps employers respond within the day as air quality changes.
